frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The imputation of fault/censure onto an agent for a deed — i.e., holding someone answerable-at-fault and expressing that as reproach/blame. The root supplies a directed evaluative act of fault-attribution (blame), independent of who directs it (another, a reciprocal group, or the self) and of whether the residue surfaces as the act, the agent doing it, or the state of being its target.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The imputation of fault/censure onto an agent for a deed — i.e., holding someone answerable-at-fault and expressing that as reproach/blame. The root supplies a directed evaluative act of fault-attribution (blame), independent of who directs it (another, a reciprocal group, or the self) and of whether the residue surfaces as the act, the agent doing it, or the state of being its target.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation:
Every occurrence resolves to the single notion "blame / reproach = imputing fault to an agent for something done."

FORM I active verb (blaming as an act): 12:32:4:1 لُمْتُنَّنِى "you (women) blamed me concerning him" (Potiphar's wife); 14:22:25:1 تَلُومُونِى "do not blame me" and 14:22:26:2 لُومُوا أَنفُسَكُم "blame your own selves" (Satan redirecting culpability). Here the root is transparently the verbal act of fault-attribution, and the same act is even turned reflexive ("blame yourselves").

FORM VI reciprocal verb (mutual blaming): 68:30:5:1 يَتَلَاوَمُونَ — the ruined garden-owners "blaming one another." Pure directed fault-attribution, now bidirectional; the VI morphology supplies the reciprocity, the root supplies the blame.

PASSIVE PARTICIPLE مَلُوم (state of being the target of blame): 17:29:12:1 and 17:39:17:1 مَلُومًا (sitting/cast down "blamed"); 23:6:10:1 & 70:30:10:1 غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ ("not blamed" re lawful spouses); 51:54:5:2 فَمَا أَنتَ بِمَلُومٍ ("you are not to be blamed"). The residue is the imputable-fault-censure whose target is either affirmed or negated.

FORM IV participle مُلِيم (agent who has brought blame upon himself / is culpable): 37:142:4:1 (Jonah, swallowed "while mulīm") and 51:40:7:1 (Pharaoh cast in the sea "while mulīm"). The IV morphology adds "having done that which incurs X"; the X is still blame — one in a state of deserved fault-censure.

ACTIVE PARTICIPLE + INSTANCE NOUN (the blamer and an act of blame): 5:54:27–28 لَوْمَةَ لَآئِمٍ "the blame of any blamer" — لَوْمَة is a single act of censure, لَآئِم the one who censures.

INTENSIVE ADJECTIVE (habitual self-reproach): 75:2:4:2 النَّفْس اللَّوَّامَة "the ever-reproaching soul" — intensive form of the same fault-imputing act, turned on the self.

Across active/reciprocal verbs, passive/active participles, instance and intensive nominals, the constant left after subtracting morphology is: directed attribution of fault = blame.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Subtractions performed to isolate the residue: (a) FORM/derivation — Form I (لام) gives the plain act of blaming; Form VI (تلاوم) adds reciprocity ("blame one another"); Form IV (ألام → مُلِيم) adds the "do/enter-into that which incurs X" causative-inchoative sense, yielding "culpable, deserving blame"; passive participle مَلُوم gives "one blamed"; active participle لَائِم gives "blamer"; instance noun لَوْمَة gives "one act of blame"; intensive adjective لَوَّامَة gives "much-/habitually-blaming." All these are morphological overlays on a constant "blame." (b) CONSTRUCTION — object-of-blame marked by فِي (لمتنني فيه "blamed me concerning him"); negation غَيْر / بِ + مَلُوم supplies "not"; genitive لَوْمَة لَائِم supplies "blame OF a blamer." These frames set the vector/polarity, not the meaning. (c) PARTICIPANTS — blamer/blamed vary (women, Satan, self, believers, Jonah, Pharaoh) with no effect on the residue. (d) CONTEXT — legal (spouses غير ملومين), eschatological (hell ملوما مدحورا; mulīm at punishment), narrative (Joseph, Jonah, Pharaoh, the garden owners), spiritual (self-reproaching soul) — all contribute setting only. Residue after all subtractions: attribution of fault/censure to an agent for a deed.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The Form IV participle مُلِيم (37:142:4:1 Jonah; 51:40:7:1 Pharaoh) is the hardest, because unlike مَلُوم ("one blamed by someone") it is not obviously a passive target of blame — no blamer is named, and Jonah/Pharaoh are described as mulīm at the very moment of divine seizure, not while being verbally reproached. It reconciles cleanly through layer-subtraction: Form IV of this root is the standard "do/become such as to incur X" pattern (cf. أذنب "commit a sin"), so مُلِيم = "one who has brought blame upon himself / stands culpable." The root residue "fault-imputable censure" is still present — it is the very thing incurred. The morphology (IV) supplies "having earned," the root supplies "blame." So it strengthens rather than breaks the unity: the residue survives even where no external blamer is present, showing the core is fault-attribution itself, not merely the social speech-act.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Strongest alternative: the core is "fault/culpability" (a state) rather than "the act of blaming." This also covers مَلُوم/مُلِيم (states of being at fault) and غَيْر مَلُومِين (not culpable). Internal arbitration favors the blame-attribution reading: the data foregrounds the ACT and its AGENT, not bare culpability — لَائِم (a blamer), لَوْمَة (a discrete act of blame), يَتَلَاوَمُون (reciprocal blaming), لُومُوا أَنفُسَكُم (imperative to perform blaming), لَوَّامَة (habitual blamer). A pure "culpability/fault" core cannot generate an agent-noun "blamer" or a reciprocal "blame each other," whereas an "act-of-fault-attribution" core generates both the act (verbs, لومة, لائم, لوامة) and the derived state (passive ملوم, IV مليم = target/incurrer of that attribution). Hence the attributive-censure reading subsumes the culpability reading, not vice versa; internal evidence arbitrates for it.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest Quranic/Arabic semantic neighbors: ذمّ (*mm, dispraise — the antonym of حمد/praise, an evaluation of intrinsic worth/quality), عذل ('*l, reproof, near-synonym, sparse), and عيّر/وبّخ (taunt/rebuke). lwm is distinct in that it imputes fault to an AGENT for a specific answerable DEED — it presupposes responsibility for an act and censures that (لمتنني فيه = blamed me concerning [a deed]; لوموا أنفسكم = hold yourselves at fault). It is agent-directed, deed-anchored, and freely reflexive/reciprocal (لوامة, تلاوم), unlike ذمّ which grades a thing's worth (praise-vs-dispraise axis) without necessarily targeting an agent's deed. Falsifiability: if any occurrence used lwm for evaluation of intrinsic worth/quality of a thing with no imputable deed and no answerable agent (i.e., as a mere antonym of "praiseworthy"), the deed-anchored fault-attribution core would be falsified and the reading would collapse toward the generic ذمّ sense.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — attribution of fault/censure to an agent for a deed (blame/reproach) — is surface-recoverable in all 14 occurrences with a determinate direction (censure aimed at a culpable agent). Every form-family transparently instantiates it: Form I active verbs (لمتنني، تلوموني، لوموا), Form VI reciprocal (يتلاومون), passive participle (ملوم/ملومين, affirmed or negated), Form IV culpability participle (مليم), active participle (لائم), instance noun (لومة), and intensive adjective (لوّامة). No occurrence requires forcing: the two genuinely different-looking cases — IV مُلِيم (state of incurred blame) and the reflexive/intensive لوّامة / لوموا أنفسكم (self-directed blame) — reconcile by ordinary morphological subtraction (IV = "having incurred X"; reflexive object = self as target) while leaving the blame-residue intact, which actually confirms that the core is fault-attribution rather than either the social speech-act alone or bare culpability alone. Direction is determinate and the root is sharply distinct from its nearest neighbor ذمّ (worth-dispraise). The unity is achieved without metaphorical stretching and without any unreconciled occurrence, warranting STRONG.

adversarial_verification.notes: Adversarial sweep of all 14 occurrences found no genuine failing occurrence. The root is semantically compact and every residue reduces to directed fault-attribution (blame/reproach). Verb (I): 12:32 لُمْتُنَّنِى, 14:22 تَلُومُونِى + reflexive لُومُوا أَنفُسَكُم = act of blaming, even redirected onto self. VI 68:30 يَتَلَاوَمُونَ = mutual blame (reciprocity is morphological). Passive participle مَلُوم 17:29/17:39 (blamed) and negated 23:6/70:30/51:54 (غير ملومين / بملوم) = target-of-blame, affirmed or negated; negation is not absence of the concept. Active participle + instance noun 5:54 لَوْمَةَ لَآئِمٍ = blamer + single act of censure. Intensive ADJ 75:2 اللَّوَّامَة = habitual self-reproach. HARDEST CASES: the two Form IV مُلِيم (37:142 Jonah, 51:40 Pharaoh), morphologically most distant — probed for a circular save. Standard lexical value of أَلاَمَ/مُليم is "having done what incurs blame → culpable"; subtracting the IV 'do-what-incurs-X' morphology leaves X = blame, so it is root-anchored, not ad hoc. DISTINCTIVENESS holds: the contribution discriminates against ذمّ (dispraise of worth/character), لعن (curse/expulsion), عذل (dissuasive reproach), and عذاب (punishment) — لوم uniquely centers the imputation of fault to an agent for a specific deed. FALSIFIABILITY holds: a clear failure condition exists (any occurrence bearing an unrelated/homonymous sense), and no occurrence meets it. Verdict SUPPORTED.

occurrence_dispositions.note: لُمْتُنَّنِى فِيهِ 'you (women) blamed me concerning him' — Form V active verb, transparent act of fault-attribution directed at the speaker by others; candidate residue (blame) fully present.
فَلَا تَلُومُونِى 'do not blame me' — Satan negating others' fault-imputation onto himself; directed evaluative blame is exactly the residue, only prohibited.
وَلُومُوا أَنفُسَكُم 'blame your own selves' — same blame act turned reflexive (self as target); root supplies fault-attribution, participants shift, residue intact.
فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُومًا 'so you sit blamed' — passive participle, the state of being target of censure for the fault (extravagance); residue present as affirmed target-state.
فَتُلْقَىٰ فِى جَهَنَّمَ مَلُومًا 'cast into Hell, blamed' — passive participle; being-blamed state for the deed (shirk); candidate residue directly recoverable.
فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ 'they are not blamed' — passive participle with negation; blame residue is what is negated (no fault imputable re lawful spouses).
وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ 'while culpable' (Jonah) — Form IV participle 'having done that which incurs blame'; IV adds the causative-incurrence, X = blame; residue recoverable via candidate's own logic.
وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ 'while culpable' (Pharaoh) — Form IV participle, one in a state of deserved fault-censure; blame residue present under IV morphology.
فَمَا أَنتَ بِمَلُومٍ 'you are not to be blamed' — passive participle negated; the fault-imputation residue is exactly what is denied of the addressee.
لَوْمَةَ لَآئِمٍ — لَوْمَة is the instance noun 'a single act of censure/blame'; directed fault-attribution as a discrete act, residue transparent.
لَآئِمٍ 'a blamer' — active participle, the agent who performs the blame act; root supplies the fault-attributing act, morphology supplies the doer.
يَتَلَاوَمُونَ 'blaming one another' — Form VI reciprocal; VI supplies bidirectionality, root supplies the blame; mutual fault-attribution among garden-owners.
غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ 'not blamed' — passive participle with negation (lawful spouses); blame residue is the negated target-state, fully recoverable.
النَّفْس اللَّوَّامَة 'the ever-reproaching soul' — intensive adjective (faʿʿāla) of the same fault-imputing act, turned habitually on the self; residue = self-directed blame.
